findings.title: Unhealthy spawn processes are never killed due to isinstance check
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive` the kill is now guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces a `SpawnProcess` that derives from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process` (the default-context class). The guard therefore evaluates False and hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is started, leaking processes that still hold Redis connections and keep flushing the same shards concurrently with the new process (duplicate/fragmented segment production). The same problem applies to `process.terminate()` in `join()` (line 346). Use `BaseProcess` or check for `threading.Thread` instead.

findings.title: join() breaks out of shutdown loop leaving remaining processes untouched
findings.body: In `join()`, when the deadline is exceeded the loop `break`s, so processes with higher indices are never waited on nor terminated. With multiple flusher processes, a timed-out shutdown can leave daemon processes alive that continue flushing segments while the consumer rebalances. `remaining_time` is also computed but unused. Terminate all processes unconditionally after the wait loop instead of breaking out.

findings.title: Dead/incorrect helper `_create_process_for_shard`
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is never called anywhere after the refactor (health checking now restarts by process index). Dead code that duplicates restart logic and has no restart-counter accounting; it should be removed to avoid future misuse that bypasses the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS guard.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards=` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `shard=`. This breaks dashboards/queries grouping on a single tag key. Also note the tag value is now a comma-joined list of shards, which changes cardinality and the meaning of existing `shard` tags on these metrics.

findings.title: time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op, so the added sleep does not wait
findings.body: `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top of the test makes the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` (and its comment about giving flusher threads time) a no-op. The test therefore still races against the flusher thread producing into `messages`, and the following `(msg,) = messages` can fail intermittently. Use a real wait/poll loop (e.g. a saved reference to the original sleep or polling until messages is non-empty).

findings.title: Multi-process flusher test only asserts bookkeeping, not behaviour
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` checks `len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes` and the shard count, but never submits spans nor verifies that segments from all 4 shards are actually flushed by the 2 workers. The core new behaviour (shard partitioning across processes, per-process backpressure/health, no duplicate or missing segments) is untested.
